text:
The term "passive movements" refers to movements of a body part produced by an external force (such as a therapist, machine, or gravity) rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. This contrasts with active movements, which are performed by the person's own muscle contraction, and with resistance/stretch movements, which involve added force. Passive movements are used in assessment (e.g., checking joint range of motion) and treatment (e.g., preventing stiffness).
